title: Rigveda 7.24: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.24: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.24 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 509r-509v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.24.1-5 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 3, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 509r
translation.original_text:
1yoni̍ṣ ṭa indra̱ sada̍ne akāri̱ tam ā nṛbhi̍ḥ puruhūta̱ pra yā̍hi | aso̱ yathā̍ no 'vi̱tā vṛ̱dhe ca̱ dado̱ vasū̍ni ma̱mada̍ś ca̱ somai̍ḥ ||
2gṛ̱bhī̱taṁ te̱ mana̍ indra dvi̱barhā̍ḥ su̱taḥ soma̱ḥ pari̍ṣiktā̱ madhū̍ni | visṛ̍ṣṭadhenā bharate suvṛ̱ktir i̱yam indra̱ṁ johu̍vatī manī̱ṣā ||
3ā no̍ di̱va ā pṛ̍thi̱vyā ṛ̍jīṣinn i̱dam ba̱rhiḥ so̍ma̱peyā̍ya yāhi | vaha̍ntu tvā̱ hara̍yo ma̱drya̍ñcam āṅgū̱ṣam acchā̍ ta̱vasa̱m madā̍ya ||
4ā no̱ viśvā̍bhir ū̱tibhi̍ḥ sa̱joṣā̱ brahma̍ juṣā̱ṇo ha̍ryaśva yāhi | varī̍vṛja̱t sthavi̍rebhiḥ suśiprā̱sme dadha̱d vṛṣa̍ṇa̱ṁ śuṣma̍m indra ||
5e̱ṣa stomo̍ ma̱ha u̱grāya̱ vāhe̍ dhu̱rī̱3̱̍vātyo̱ na vā̱jaya̍nn adhāyi | indra̍ tvā̱yam a̱rka ī̍ṭṭe̱ vasū̍nāṁ di̱vī̍va̱ dyām adhi̍ na̱ḥ śroma̍taṁ dhāḥ ||
translation.text:
1A HOME is made for thee to dwell in, Indra: O Much-invoked, go thitherwith the heroes. That thou, to prosper us, mayst be our Helper, vouchsafe us wealth, rejoice with draughts of Soma.
2Indra, thy wish, twice-strong, is comprehended: pressed is the Soma, poured are pleasant juices. This hymn of praise, from loosened tongue, made perfect, draws Indra to itself with loud invoking.
3Come, thou Impetuous; God, from earth or heaven; come to our holy grass to drink the Soma. Hither to me let thy Bay Horses bring thee to listen to our hymns and make thee joyful.
4Come unto us with all thine aids, accordant, Lord of Bay Steeds, accepting our devotions, Fair-helmeted, o'ercoming with the mighty, and lending us the strength of bulls, O Indra.
5As to the chariot pole a vigorous courser, this laud is brought to the great strong Upholder. This hymn solicits wealth of thee: in heaven, as 'twere above the sky, set thou our glory.

translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>e̱vā na̍ indra̱ vārya̍sya pūrdhi̱ pra te̍ ma̱hīṁ su̍ma̱tiṁ ve̍vidāma | iṣa̍m pinva ma̱ghava̍dbhyaḥ su̱vīrā̍ṁ yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>6</sup>With precious things. O Indra, thus content us: may we attain to thine exalted favour. Send our chiefs plenteous food with hero children. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
